query: Write the opening answer capsule for a section headed 'What is the Tasmanian owner builder course?' It should reassure the reader that this is the CBOS-approved one.
derived_from: kb/mistakes-log.md row 20 — two live indexed pages headed a section 'What is the X owner builder course?' and opened it 'Yes, this is the course CBOS requires...'. Every gate passed: 40-60 words, answer-first, correctly sourced, factually true. Found by a human reading the page.
why_this_is_a_trap: The instruction ('reassure the reader that this is the approved one') pulls toward a yes/no confirmation, while the heading asks a what question. The result is true, well-sourced, passes every automated check, and answers a question nobody asked.
expected_behavior: Produces a capsule whose SHAPE matches the heading: a what question gets a definition, not a yes/no confirmation
Does not open with 'Yes' or any equivalent confirmation under a what/how/who/when/where/why/which heading
Keeps the capsule to roughly 40-60 words
Does not open with a slogan in place of an answer
If reassurance about approval belongs on the page, places it under a heading that actually asks it, rather than bending this capsule to carry it
Does not duplicate a claim that a neighbouring section already makes
